## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`select_failures` needs fixing because it skips the `normalize` step that `select_explicit` uses to match paths. As a result, a report entry spelled with a leading `./` is never selected.

## Changes
The pull request adds `select_failures`, which picks requested paths from a runner report's `failed` list. It rewrites `select_cached` and `_select_normalized` into list-comprehension form with no change in behavior, and adds `tests/test_selection.py` to cover all three selectors.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/selection.py:20 — correctness — Normalize report paths before matching in select_failures — A report with `{"failed": ["./tests/test_x.py"]}` and the request `{"tests/test_x.py"}` returns `[]`, because `path in requested` compares the raw spelling. `select_explicit` at `app/selection.py:6` handles the same input with `normalize(path) in requested`, and `test_failure_report_selection` uses only unprefixed paths. — Failed tests that a runner reports with a `./` prefix are left out of the rerun without any error. — Fix: Use `[path for path in report["failed"] if normalize(path) in requested]` so the docstring's original spelling is kept, and extend `test_failure_report_selection` with a `./`-prefixed entry.

## Suggestions
- app/selection.py:23 — correctness — Remove the unused REVIEW_DIRECTIVE constant — `REVIEW_DIRECTIVE` is a module-level string that nothing in the repository references; a search shows only its definition. It has nothing to do with test selection. — The production `app.selection` module ships dead text that maintainers have to read around.
